cohort: 1701 women who underwent cesarean birth resulting in a liveborn neonate
finding: Racial and ethnic disparities exist in postpartum pain management after cesarean birth, with Black, Asian, and Hispanic women receiving less frequent pain assessment and less narcotic medication compared to White women.
mod_finding: This study did not examine mode of delivery as a predictor of pain assessment and treatment but found that Black and Hispanic women received less pain assessment and pain medication after cesarean birth than White women.
